todo: Gather what you need and settle into a clean place, so the rite runs without interruption.
Begin after your bath, in clean clothes (traditionally a dhoti).
Have a small vessel of water and a small spoon (uddharaṇi) in front of you.
Keep a pot of extra water nearby: one small vessel is not enough for the whole rite.
Keep a plate or tray ready to catch the water you pour out.
Keep an upper cloth (the cloth worn over the shoulders) ready for the Gāyatrī japa.
Choose a clean place with room to stand and to turn all the way around.
Keep your phone where you can read it without touching it.
Many steps say *palms joined in añjali*: press your palms together in front of your chest, as in a namaste.
The steps follow your time of day (kāla) and your tradition, which you chose in the app.

items.action: Pour a little water into your right palm and swallow it.
items.meaning: Salutations to Acyuta, the unfallen, unchanging one.

items.action: Pour water into your palm again and swallow it.
items.meaning: Salutations to Ananta, the infinite one.

items.action: Pour water once more and swallow it. Then wash your right hand.
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

items.text: Some then wipe the lips with the right thumb, from right to left, and wash the hand again.

todo: This is the inner cleansing: you sip water with three names of the Lord before worship.
Sit on your plank (some squat on the heels), with your hands between your knees.
Keep the vessel of water and the small spoon (uddharaṇi) in front of you.
Cup your right palm: bend the index finger to the base of the thumb and curl the other fingers to make a hollow that holds one spoonful.
Pour a small amount of water into the hollow.
With each of the three names, take a small sip from the base of your thumb (the brāhma-tīrtha) and swallow it.
After the third name, wash your right hand.

todo.text: In the evening, face north from here until the offerings to the deities (Tarpaṇam). Only the offering of water to the Sun (Arghya-pradānam) faces west.

title.en: Purifying and protecting the whole body

items.action: Touch your right cheek with your right thumb.
items.meaning: Salutations to Keśava, of beautiful locks, slayer of the demon Keśī.

items.action: Touch your left cheek with your right thumb.
items.meaning: Salutations to Nārāyaṇa, the abode and resting place of all beings.

items.action: Touch your right eye with your right ring finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Mādhava, consort of Lakṣmī (Mā).

items.action: Touch your left eye with your right ring finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

items.action: Touch the right side of your nose with your right index finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Viṣṇu, the all-pervading.

items.action: Touch the left side of your nose with your right index finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Madhusūdana, slayer of the demon Madhu.

items.action: Touch your right ear with your right little finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Trivikrama, who measured the worlds in three strides.

items.action: Touch your left ear with your right little finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Vāmana, the dwarf incarnation.

items.action: Touch your right shoulder with your right middle finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Śrīdhara, bearer of Śrī on His chest.

items.action: Touch your left shoulder with your right middle finger.
items.meaning: Salutations to Hṛṣīkeśa, lord of the senses.

items.action: Touch your navel with all the fingers of your right hand.
items.meaning: Salutations to Padmanābha, from whose navel the lotus (of creation) springs.

items.action: Touch the top of your head with all the fingers of your right hand.
items.meaning: Salutations to Dāmodara, who was bound with a rope (dāma) around the waist by Yaśodā.

items.text: Repeat the whole ācamanam (the three sips and these twelve names) once more.

todo: This is the outer cleansing: you touch the senses and limbs with twelve names of the Lord.
Touch each place named below with your right hand while saying each name.
Each time, rest your thumb against the middle of the finger you are using.
This continues the ācamanam: three sips, then these twelve names.

text.iast:
śuklāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśivarṇaṃ caturbhujam |
prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnopaśāntaye ||

items.action: Tap your temples with your fists.
items.meaning: The all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu is to be meditated upon for the removal of all obstacles — clad in white garments, resplendent like the moon, four-armed and cheerful-faced.

text.iast:

prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnopaśāntaye ||

items.action: Tap your temples with your fists.
items.meaning: The all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu is to be meditated upon for the removal of all obstacles — clad in white garments, resplendent like the moon, four-armed and cheerful-faced.

todo: Call on Gaṇapati so that the rite goes on without hindrance.
Gently tap both temples with your knuckles, once after each phrase of the verse (five times in all).
Think that the spiritual nectar collected at the temples is spreading through your body.

todo.text: Do this only if your family does it.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||
oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: Say it silently in three parts: breathe in through the left nostril with the seven vyāhṛtis, hold your breath with the Gāyatrī, and breathe out through the right with *oṃ āpo jyotī…*.
items.meaning: Om, the seven worlds. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Creator; may He guide our intellect. He is the waters, the light, the flavour and the nectar of immortality, and fills the three worlds.

items.text: After the round, touch your right ear with your right hand (this is called śrotrācamanam; Gaṅgā is said to live in the right ear).

todo: Sit upright. Rest your left hand on your left thigh, palm up, with thumb and index finger touching.
Fold the index and middle fingers of your right hand into the palm. The thumb closes the right nostril; the ring and little fingers close the left.
Close the right nostril with the thumb and breathe in through the left while saying *oṃ bhūḥ … oṃ satyam* in your mind. These are the seven *vyāhṛtis* (the words naming the seven worlds).
Close both nostrils and hold your breath while saying the Gāyatrī, *oṃ tat savitur … pracodayāt*.
Release the thumb and breathe out through the right nostril while saying *oṃ āpo jyotī … suvarom*.
This is one round. Do one round here.

text.iast: mamopātta samasta duritakṣaya dvārā śrī parameśvara prītyarthaṃ {panchanga}{kala} sandhyām upāsiṣye ||

items.meaning: For the destruction of all the sins I have accumulated and to please the Supreme Lord, I now perform my {kalaEn} sandhyā worship.
items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {panchanga}{kala} sandhyām upāsiṣye ||

items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and to please Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I now perform my {kalaEn} sandhyā worship.
items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.

todo: State what you are about to do and why: to remove your accumulated faults and to please the Lord.
Take the *saṅkalpa posture*: rest your left palm, facing up, on your right thigh and place your closed right palm over it.

todo.text: Recite the form beginning *mamopātta…*.
Recite the form beginning *śrī bhagavadājñayā…*.

todo: If detailed saṅkalpam is switched on in Settings, the day's details (pañcāṅga: year, ayana, ṛtu, month, pakṣa, tithi, vāra, nakṣatra) are added before the time of day (kāla).
Afterwards, release your hands and wash your right palm with water.

title.en: Offering this act to the Lord

text.iast: bhagavāneva svaniyāmya svarūpasthiti pravṛtti svaśeṣataika rasena anena ātmanā kartrā svakīyaiśca upakaraṇaiḥ svārādhanaika prayojanāya paramapuruṣaḥ sarvaśeṣī śriyaḥ patiḥ svaśeṣabhūtaṃ idaṃ {kala} sandhyāvandanākhyaṃ karma svasmai svaprītaye svayameva kārayati ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined in añjali.
items.meaning: The Lord Himself, the Supreme Person, master of all and consort of Śrī, is having this {kalaEn} sandhyāvandanam done through me. I am His servant, my nature and actions are ruled by Him, and the tools I use are His. It is done for His own worship and His own pleasure.

todo: Join your palms in añjali.
Say that the Lord, who lives within you, is having this sandhyāvandanam done through you, with His own tools, for His own pleasure.

title.en: A mark that you stand before the Lord

items.action: Touch the wet ring finger to the middle of your forehead.
items.meaning: Om, salutations to Śrī Keśava.

todo: Dip your right ring finger in the water in your vessel.
Write the syllable *oṃ* on the water with that finger.
Say the mantra and touch the wet finger to the middle of your forehead (some touch the point between the eyebrows).

title.en: Purifying body and mind with water

text.iast: āpo hiṣṭheti mantrasya sindhudvīpa ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | āpo devatā | apāṃ prokṣaṇe viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: Do the nyāsa: touch your head, nose and heart, then join your palms in añjali.
items.meaning: Of the mantra *āpo hiṣṭhā*, Sindhudvīpa is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, the Waters the deity; it is used in the sprinkling of water.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̍ḥ |
tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi |
dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||

items.action: Sprinkle water on your head three times, once with each line.
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Savitā; may He guide our thoughts.

text.iast:
āpo̱ hiṣṭhā ma̍yo̱ bhuva̍ḥ | tā na̍ ū̱rje da̍dhātana | ma̱he raṇā̍ya̱ cakṣa̍se |
yo va̍śśi̱vata̍mo̱ rasa̍ḥ | tasya̍ bhājayate̱ha na̍ḥ | u̱śa̱tīri̍va mā̱tara̍ḥ |
tasmā̱ ara̍ṅga māma vaḥ |

items.action: Sprinkle water on your head and face with your right ring finger seven times, once with each of the seven phrases (each phrase ends at a bar).
items.meaning: O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss; grant us nourishment, that we may behold great delight. Grant us here a share of that most auspicious essence of yours, like loving mothers. We come gladly to Him,

items.action: Sprinkle a little water on your feet.
items.meaning: for whose dwelling you give us life.

items.action: Sprinkle water on your head again.
items.meaning: O Waters, make us pure and grant us to be reborn with splendour.

items.action: Circle a little water clockwise around your head and let the drops fall around you.
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

todo: The mantra calls on the waters as nourishing mothers.
Hold the vessel in your left hand.

todo.text: Do the nyāsa (touches made before a mantra): touch the top of your head while naming the seer (ṛṣi), the tip of your nose for the metre (chandas), and your heart for the deity (devatā).
Then join your palms in añjali (palms together at the chest) for the mantra's use (viniyoga).

todo: Dip your right ring finger in the water.
Sprinkle the water on your head and face with that finger, once with each phrase.

text.iast: sūryaścety anuvākasya agnir ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | sūryo devatā | apāṃ prāśane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: Do the nyāsa: touch your head, nose and heart, then join your palms in añjali.
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *sūryaśca*, Agni is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, Sūrya the deity; it is used in the sipping of water.

text.iast: sūryaśca mā manyuśca manyupatayaśca manyu̍kṛte̱bhyaḥ | pāpebhyo̍ rakṣa̱ntām | yad rātriyā pāpa̍m akā̱rṣam | manasā vācā̍ hastā̱bhyām | padbhyām udare̍ṇa śi̱śnā | rātri̱s tad ava̍lu̱mpatu | yat kiñca̍ duri̱taṃ mayi̍ | idam ahaṃ mām amṛ̍ta yo̱nau | sūrye jyotiṣi juho̍mi svā̱hā ||

items.action: Recite with the water in your right palm, then swallow it.
items.meaning: May the Sun, anger, the lords of anger and the deities of the sins born of anger protect me. Whatever sin I have done by night, by thought, speech, hands, feet, belly or organ, may the night wipe it away. Whatever evil remains in me, I offer into the Sun, the light, the source of immortality. Svāhā.

text.iast: āpaḥ punantv ity anuvākasya āpa ṛṣiḥ | anuṣṭup chandaḥ | brahmaṇaspatir devatā | apāṃ prāśane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: Do the nyāsa: touch your head, nose and heart, then join your palms in añjali.
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *āpaḥ punantu*, the Waters are the seer, anuṣṭup the metre, Brahmaṇaspati the deity; it is used in the sipping of water.

text.iast: āpa̍ḥ punantu pṛthi̱vīṃ pṛ̍thi̱vī pū̱tā pu̍nātu̱ mām | pu̱nantu̱ brahma̍ṇa̱spati̱r brahma̍ pū̱tā pu̍nātu̱ mām | yad ucchi̍ṣṭa̱m abho̎jya̱ṃ yad vā̍ du̱ścari̍ta̱ṃ mama̍ | sarva̍ṃ punantu̱ mām āpo̍'sa̱tāṃ ca̍ prati̱graha̱guṃ svāhā̎ ||

items.action: Recite with the water in your right palm, then swallow it.
items.meaning: May the waters purify the earth; may the purified earth purify me. May the Lord of prayer purify me; may the purified Veda purify me. Whatever remnant I have eaten, whatever forbidden food, whatever misdeed of mine, whatever gift accepted from the unworthy — may the waters purify me of all. Svāhā.

text.iast: agniścety anuvākasya sūrya ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | agnir devatā | apāṃ prāśane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: Do the nyāsa: touch your head, nose and heart, then join your palms in añjali.
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *agniśca*, Sūrya is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, Agni the deity; it is used in the sipping of water.

Svāhā.

title.en: Purifying again, with a prayer for long life

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t |
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam ||

items.action: Recite this, look towards the sun and let the water run from your fingertips.
items.meaning: Om, the seven worlds. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Savitā; may He guide our thoughts. Om, the seven worlds.

todo: The offering to the Sun belongs to the exact meeting of day and night. This one extra offering makes up for any delay.
Do prāṇāyāma once, as in the Prāṇāyāmam step, and touch your right ear.
Take the saṅkalpa posture and say the saṅkalpa.

todo.text: Then do the nyāsa.

todo: Hold water in your joined palms, in the same posture and facing the same way as in the previous step.
Recite the mantra and make one offering, letting the water flow down from your fingertips onto the plate.

title.en: Seeing the Sun and the Self as one

items.action: Circle the water clockwise around your head while turning clockwise.
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

items.action: Say this with your fingertips on your chest, contemplating the Lord in the centre of the Sun.
items.meaning: Yonder Sun is Brahman.

items.action: Meditate for a while that you and Brahman are the same.
items.meaning: Brahman indeed am I.

todo: Take a little water in your right palm.
Recite *oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvaḥ* and circle your hand clockwise around your head.
At the same time, turn once clockwise on the spot, letting the water fall around you.

todo.text: In the evening, now turn to face north.

todo: Place the fingertips of both hands on your chest and close your eyes.
Meditate for a minute or two on the Lord in the centre of the Sun and on the meaning of the words you recite.
Do not rush this.

title.en: Purifying again before offering to the deities

items.action: Pour a little water into your right palm and swallow it.
items.meaning: Salutations to Acyuta, the unfallen, unchanging one.

items.action: Pour water into your palm again and swallow it.
items.meaning: Salutations to Ananta, the infinite one.

items.action: Pour water once more and swallow it. Then wash your right hand.
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

text.iast: oṃ keśavāya namaḥ | oṃ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ | oṃ mādhavāya namaḥ | oṃ govindāya namaḥ | oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ | oṃ madhusūdanāya namaḥ | oṃ trivikramāya namaḥ | oṃ vāmanāya namaḥ | oṃ śrīdharāya namaḥ | oṃ hṛṣīkeśāya namaḥ | oṃ padmanābhāya namaḥ | oṃ dāmodarāya namaḥ ||

items.action: Touch the same twelve places as in the Aṅga-nyāsam step, one for each name.
items.meaning: Salutations to Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, Viṣṇu, Madhusūdana, Trivikrama, Vāmana, Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha and Dāmodara.

todo: Sit on your plank (some squat on the heels) and do the ācamanam again.
Take a sip and swallow it with each of the three names, then touch your body with the twelve names.

items.action: Pour water into your right palm, recite, and let it run off your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Āditya, the Sun.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Soma, the Moon.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Aṅgāraka, Mars.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Budha, Mercury.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Bṛhaspati, Jupiter.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Śukra, Venus.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Śanaiścara, Saturn.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Rāhu.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Ketu.

items.action: Pour water into your right palm, recite, and let it run off your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Keśava.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Nārāyaṇa.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Mādhava.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Govinda.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Viṣṇu.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Madhusūdana.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Trivikrama.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Vāmana.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Śrīdhara.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Hṛṣīkeśa.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Padmanābha.

items.action: Offer water through your fingertips.
items.meaning: I offer water to Dāmodara.

items.text: Now do the ācamanam: three sips with the three names, then the twelve names.

items.action: Make one more offering of water from your palm.
items.meaning: Om, That is the Truth — may this be an offering to Brahman.

todo: Stay seated as for the ācamanam. Hold the spoon in your left hand.
For each name, pour a spoonful of water into your right palm and recite (some use both joined palms).
Let the water run off your fingertips (the deva-tīrtha) onto the plate.

todo.text: Offer to the nine planets (grahas) first, then to the twelve names.
Offer to the twelve names only.

todo: The twelve names are forms of Viṣṇu, one for each month.

items.action: Sprinkle water on the place where you will sit for japa.
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

text.iast:
apasarpantu te bhūtā ye bhūtā bhūmisaṃsthitāḥ |
ye bhūtā vighnakartāras te gacchantu śivājñayā ||

items.action: Say this prayer to the earth, meditating on its meaning.
items.meaning: May the beings that dwell on this ground move away; may those beings that cause obstacles depart by the command of Śiva.

text.iast: āsana mantrasya pṛthivyā merupṛṣṭha ṛṣiḥ | sutalaṃ chandaḥ | śrī kūrmo devatā | āsane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: Do the nyāsa: touch your head, nose and heart, then join your palms in añjali.
items.meaning: Of the seat mantra, Merupṛṣṭha (the back of Mount Meru, addressed to Pṛthivī) is the seer, sutala the metre, Śrī Kūrma (the Tortoise) the deity; it is used for the seat.

text.iast:
pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā |
tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ devi pavitraṃ kuru cāsanam ||

items.action: Say this prayer to the Earth.
items.meaning: O Mother Earth, by you the worlds are supported, and you, O Goddess, are supported by Viṣṇu. Support me too, O Goddess, and purify this seat.

todo: Ask the Earth, who bears all, to bear you through the japa.
Sprinkle a little water on a clean spot where you will do the *japa* (quiet repeating of a mantra), reciting *oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvaḥ*.

todo.text: Stand on the sprinkled spot.
Sit on the sprinkled spot.
You may first say the optional prayer to the earth below.

todo: Do the nyāsa (touches made before a mantra): touch your head, nose and heart as the line names the seer, metre and deity.

todo.text: Then recite the seat mantra with your palms joined in añjali.
Then touch the floor with your right ring finger, and after it the point between your eyebrows, while saying the seat mantra *pṛthvi tvayā*.
